en: The Chapter on Similes, Section on the Monkey.
9. The Question on the Factors of the Fisherman “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘two factors of a fisherman should be adopted,’ which are those two factors that should be adopted?
“Just as, Great King, a fisherman draws up fish with a hook;”
In the same way, Great King, the practitioner of yoga, the yogāvacara, should extract the further fruits of recluseship by means of knowledge.
This, Great King, is the first quality to be adopted from the fisherman.
Furthermore, Great King, the fisherman, having killed a small [fish], attains a vast profit.
In the same way, Great King, the practitioner of yoga, the yogāvacara, must relinquish even a small amount of worldly bait.
Having relinquished a small amount of worldly bait, Great King, the yogī, the yogāvacara, attains the vast fruit of recluseship.
This, Great King, is the second quality to be adopted from the fisherman.
This was also said, Great King, by the Elder Rāhula:
and the liberation that is desireless;”
"Having abandoned the bait of the world, one attains the four fruits and the six direct knowledges.
Thus ends the ninth question, on the parts of a fisherman.
